candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — central-line infection prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Apply CDC-supported central-line infection-prevention practices: aseptic technique, maximal sterile barriers, appropriate chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, and prompt removal when the line is no longer essential.

options.A: Use maximal sterile barriers for insertion, appropriate chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, hand hygiene and site care, and promptly remove the catheter when it is no longer essential.
options.B: Replace all central lines routinely every 24 hours regardless of indication, site condition, or ongoing clinical need.
options.C: Apply topical antibiotic ointment routinely to every central-line insertion site and omit sterile barriers during insertion.
options.D: Keep unnecessary central venous catheters in place until discharge because repeated insertion is always riskier than prolonged dwell time.

candidate.rationale: CDC central-line guidance recommends maximal sterile barrier precautions for CVC/PICC insertion, skin preparation with greater than 0.5% chlorhexidine in alcohol when not contraindicated, hand hygiene and aseptic catheter care, and prompt removal of intravascular catheters that are no longer essential. Routine replacement of CVCs to prevent infection is not recommended. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC supports maximal sterile barriers, chlorhexidine-alcohol skin preparation, hand hygiene/aseptic care, and prompt removal of unnecessary central catheters as infection-prevention measures.
